  You are revising ADR-0014 at D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/adr-0014-geometry-broadphase-and-occluder-source-seam.md (project D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d, Godot 4.7.2 GDScript) after per-ADR engine and TD-ADR reviews and a cross-ADR adjudication of the Core tier.   ADR-0014 review verdict CONCERNS:
  E1 [high, BLOCKING] As written, QueryBuffer will not load under the project's warning policy. The Key Interfaces block declares `func _init(capacity: int) -> void` and `func capacity() -> int` in the same class. ADR-0010 sets SHADOWED_VARIABLE=2, and I probed this on 4.7.2 (headless, project warnings at 2): `Parse Error: The local function parameter "capacity" is shadowing an already-declared function at line 7 in the current class. (Warning treated as error.)` Loading returns an unusable script (can_instantiate false). Every consumer (Body, Emitter, Lighting, tests) constructs this class, so the fault is on the critical path. Probe: C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/adr-probes/review-ADR-0014/src/qb_a.gd.
    amendment: Change the constructor to `func _init(initial_capacity: int) -> void`. `capacity()` can stay. Add a line to the Key Interfaces note saying that parameter, local and member names in these classes must not shadow any method of the same class (SHADOWED_VARIABLE=2 includes functions). Check the other listed classes for the same pattern, for example a local `version` inside LayoutVersions or the adapters.
  E2 [medium] LayoutVersions is specified (section 6) as holding three PackedInt64Array columns named `version`, `static_version` and `leaf_version`. Section 9 and the Guidelines also tag `LayoutVersions` getters `## @hot`, and the ports and adapters expose `version(section_id)`, `static_version(...)` and `leaf_version(...)`. If the getters keep those names on the same class as the columns, GDScript rejects it. I probed a class with `var version: PackedInt64Array` and `func version(section_id)`: `Parse Error: Function "version" has the same name as a previously declared variable.` The Key Interfaces block lists no getters for LayoutVersions, so the clash is left to the implementer. A second hazard is that getters on those columns index by section_id, and an out-of-range packed-array index is an engine script error rather than a 0. The ADR's `0 = no such live section` therefore needs an explicit bounds check. In my OOB probe the headless run did not exit within 120 s; I did not isolate why, so that part is UNVERIFIED.
    amendment: Name the columns with a private prefix (`_version_col`, `_static_col`, `_leaf_col`). Add the getters (`version_of(section_id) -> int` and so on) to the Key Interfaces block, each with an explicit `if section_id < 0 or section_id >= _version_col.size(): return 0` guard, and tag them `## @hot`.
  E3 [medium] The V1 'probed' claim about `PackedByteArray.find` is wrong for negative starts. The ADR says it 'returns -1 ... for a negative `from`'. On 4.7.2 with b=[0,1,0,1], `find(1,-1)` returns 3 and `find(1,-3)` returns 1: a negative start counts from the end of the array. `find(1,4)` returned -1 (start at the size), as claimed. The ADR's conclusion (never pass a negative start) is right, but the stated reason is not. A bug that passes a negative start would return a wrong in-range index with no -1 sentinel. Only fallback rung 4 uses `find`, so this is not blocking.
    amendment: Rewrite V1 to say: 'find(value, from) with from < 0 is end-relative and can return a valid wrong index; from >= size returns -1'. In rung 4, require a `pos >= 0` guard in code and in the corpus test. Do not describe the negative case as returning -1.
  E4 [low] Several Key Interfaces stubs use `: ...` as a function body (`func _init(capacity: int) -> void: ...`, `func grow(min_capacity: int) -> void: ...` and others). That is not valid GDScript. Probed: `Parse Error: Expected statement, found "..." instead.` The ADR says 'bodies are the Layout epic's', but the same block is described as the contract and is likely to be pasted into stories. The `@abstract func ...` declarations without bodies are valid.
    amendment: Add 'pseudo-code: `: ...` marks an elided body and is a parse error if pasted' to the note under Key Interfaces. Alternatively use `pass` or a `push_error` stub in the non-abstract classes.
  E5 [info] V6 (UNUSED_PARAMETER on @abstract methods) is answerable now, on the 4.7.2 editor binary with every relevant warning at 2. A single-line `@abstract class_name PortA extends RefCounted` plus `@abstract func solid_in(body_id: int, ax0: int, ay0: int, ax1: int, ay1: int, out: QbC) -> int` loads cleanly, so the `@abstract class_name` one-line form is valid and the ports need no `_` prefix. A concrete override that does not use every parameter does fail: `The parameter "body_id" is never used in the function "solid_in()"`. The 4.7 typed-return rule is confirmed. An override `func version(section_id: int):` with a `pass` body fails with `Not all code paths return a value`, and an override without `-> int` is also hit by the untyped-declaration warning. So the ADR's 'restate -> T and return on every path' is correct. Consequence: any implementation that lives in src/ (the two adapters use all their parameters; Horror's or Body's own implementations may not) needs `_`-prefixed unused parameters. Doubles under tests/ are exempt via directory_rules.
    amendment: Record the V6 outcome in the Verification Required row (done, editor binary) and tell ADR-0010 section 1.2. Add one sentence to section 5: 'ports keep plain parameter names; src/ implementations prefix unused parameters with `_`'.
  E6 [low] The grid columns are PackedInt32Array and the sentinels (0x3FFFFFFF) sit near the int32 edge. Packed element writes truncate silently: probed, writing 0x1_0000_0005 into a PackedInt32Array element stored 5 with no error or warning. The ADR relies on WORLD_COORD_LIMIT keeping coordinates far from the sentinels, but nothing in `set_extent`/`set_empty`/rebuild checks the limit. A coordinate corrupted this way would silently match the empty sentinel or a wrong cell. `set_extent` and `set_empty` are marked 'hot' in a comment but have no `## @hot` tag, and they are missing from the Guidelines tag list, which disagrees with section 9's HOT-01 claim.
    amendment: Add a debug-build check `slot_extent_outside_footprint` or `coord_out_of_range` that tests `abs(v) <= WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` on every `rebuild_body` input and every `set_extent`. Add a BOOT invariant that WORLD_COORD_LIMIT is below the sentinel. Tag `set_extent` and `set_empty` `## @hot` and list them in the Guidelines.
  E7 [info] Plausibility of the section 11 'probed' figures. I did not rerun the benchmark, so the wall-clock numbers are UNVERIFIED by me. They are plausible for GDScript: about 50 ns per brute-force rect over 2,000 rects, 0.19 us per static `floor_div` call, and 0.19 us per typed port call. They are correctly labelled editor-binary and not a pass. Two points are weak. (1) The +38,400 B MEMORY_STATIC delta is said to be 'consistent with growth past 64 records', but 38,400/25 = 1,536 records, which is more than the average of 443 results; `grow(min_capacity)` leaves the growth policy (exact n versus geometric) unspecified. (2) MEMORY_STATIC and OBJECT_COUNT are blind to transient allocation (ADR-0010 P7: 100,000 freed arrays moved it by 208 bytes), so the '0 bytes over 20,000 queries' result shows no retained growth and nothing more. 'Allocates nothing per call' rests on the HOT-01 token scan, and `.slice(`, `.sort_custom(` and PackedXArray( are in that list. The verified claims are the alias write-through on a RefCounted member (is_same and write-through confirmed; a later `resize` through the member is also visible via the old alias, size 10), `resize` returning an int Error (0) that is ignorable under RETURN_VALUE_DISCARDED=0, and `>>` on a runtime negative int being arithmetic (-49 >> 4 = -4).
    amendment: State the `grow` policy (recommend geometric: max(min_capacity, capacity*2)) and say which of the 38,400 B is stamp/cand versus buffer. Reword the MEMORY_STATIC line to 'no retained growth'. Add a note that the section 3 step 6 'aliases after the check' rule is a style rule (resize is visible through the alias), not a correctness requirement. Keep the S1 caveats.
  E8 [info] Engine gotchas to add to the Implementation Guidelines. (a) GDScript `>>`/`<<` reject negative constant operands at parse time (`Invalid operands for bit shifting. Only positive operands are supported`), although variable operands work and are arithmetic at runtime. Rung 2 or any power-of-two cell-size shortcut for negative body-frame coordinates must use a variable or `IntMath.floor_div`, not a literal. Key decode `>> 12` is safe because keys are positive. (b) PackedXArray locals and members are shared by reference in script classes (probed), but copy on assignment from native properties. `QueryBuffer` and BodyGrid are script classes, so the aliasing is safe, but do not pass `out.keys` to a native method that takes the array by value inside a hot function. (c) No Object-method name clashes found. `grow`, `clear`, `capacity`, `count`, `status`, `keys`, `query`, `setup`, `set_extent` and `set_empty` do not collide with Object or RefCounted. (d) `const OK: int = 0` does not trigger SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER under warnings at 2 (probed, qb_b.gd loaded). (e) There are no const-of-constructed-object cases and no typed-collection usage in the interfaces. The `PackedInt64Array()` defaults are var initialisers, which is fine.
    amendment: Add (a) and (b) as one-line guardrails under Implementation Guidelines. No change needed for (c) to (e).
  
  ADR-0014 review verdict CONCERNS:
  T1 [HIGH, BLOCKING] ADR-0015 consumes a different QueryBuffer than ADR-0014 defines. ADR-0015 § 5.1 (line 242) and § Related (line 796) call `solid_in_into(body_id, ...)` and assume four separate `PackedInt32Array` columns `x0, y0, x1, y1`, body frame, HALF-OPEN. ADR-0014 § 4 and Key Interfaces define `solid_in(...)` and one interleaved `spans` column holding OCCUPIED spans `(x0, y0, x1-1, y1-1)`. ADR-0014 matches TR-section-015 and Layout GDD LY-12 b/e. There are three differences: the method name, the column shape and the span convention. The span convention is a correctness hazard. ADR-0015's sweep computes `ov(r)` on half-open boxes, so if `LayoutCollide` reads `spans[4k+2]` as `x1`, every SOLID rectangle shrinks by 1 px on its high edges. An actor could then enter a wall by one pixel, and two abutting hull rects would leave a 1-px seam. ADR-0014 also records the wrong assumption the other way: its cross-ADR text on ADR-0015 says 'LocomotionStep takes a SolidQuery and passes the actor's body_id', but ADR-0015 has LocomotionStep take a Body-owned `CollideSource` (`query_into(ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out)`, bound to a body) that wraps the Layout query. That is why ADR-0014's validation line 'FakeCollide extends SolidQuery drives a headless LocomotionStep' cannot be executed as written.
    amendment: In ADR-0014 § 4, add one sentence fixing the conversion every half-open consumer must use: `x1 = spans[4k+2] + 1`, `y1 = spans[4k+3] + 1`. State that `solid_in` is the canonical name and that `solid_in_into` in ADR-0015 and the GDDs is synced to it. Correct the ADR-0015 assumption and the § Architecture Diagram to 'Body via LayoutCollide (ADR-0015 CollideSource adapter, holds a SolidQuery and the bound body_id)'. Reword the § Validation 'Ports' line to: '`FakeSolidQuery extends SolidQuery` drives ADR-0015's `LayoutCollide`, and a contract test runs `LayoutCollide` against the real `LayoutSolidQuery`'. Rename the double so it cannot be confused with ADR-0015's CollideSource doubles. The ADR-0015 side is in cross_adr.
  T2 [HIGH, BLOCKING] ADR-0018 § Related (line 413) assumes that `rects_in` and `section_rects_into` return OCCLUDES_LIGHT rectangles 'as half-open integers ... no shift is applied by Layout'. ADR-0014 returns occupied (closed) spans. ADR-0017 D8.2 already reads `out.spans` correctly as occupied spans and builds the doubled closed box `[2*x0-1, 2*(x1-1)+1]` from them. If ADR-0018 is implemented as worded, the Lighting occluder polygons are built 1 px smaller than the boxes the Emitter tests. That breaks the 'one set, one lattice' consistency ADR-0018 exists to guarantee: a 1-px light leak at every wall edge, which is exactly the sim/render disagreement Pillar 1 forbids. ADR-0014 lists ADR-0018 as 'No constraint', so neither side caught the mismatch.
    amendment: Replace ADR-0014's 'ADR-0018: No constraint' cross-ADR line with: 'ADR-0018 and ADR-0028 read `spans` as occupied spans; a polygon corner is at `(x0, y0)` and `(x1_occ + 1, y1_occ + 1)`; Layout applies no shift.' ADR-0018's wording is amended to match ADR-0017 D8.2 (cross_adr).
  T3 [MEDIUM, BLOCKING] ADR-0034 cannot build entity ids or sprites from `section_rects_into` as it is specified. ADR-0034 line 231 and its assumption block expect rows that carry `idx`, flags and the current extent in SECTION-LOCAL px. ADR-0014 § 5 deliberately answers in the BODY frame (stated as an exception) and returns `keys`, not `idx`. The port offers `section_of_key` but no `idx_of_key`, and the stride is Layout tuning that `QueryBuffer` does not know. With `/` and `%` banned outside IntMath, a presenter has no sanctioned way to recover `idx` for `layout_local(section_id, kind_ordinal, idx)`. The kind (JAMB, PLATE, LEAF) is likewise not in the flags byte; ADR-0034 must derive it from the reserved idx ranges of GDD line 741. The PROJECTOR epic's sprite story is not implementable from the Key Interfaces as written.
    amendment: Add `@abstract func idx_of_key(key: int) -> int` to `OccluderSource`, implemented with `IntMath` against the stride. Add one sentence to § 5 stating that `section_rects_into` rows are body-frame, so a section-scene consumer subtracts `section_offset_x/_y(section_id)`. State that rows whose current extent is empty are omitted, so a fully retracted leaf has no row and its sprite must be hidden by the consumer. The ADR-0034 side is in cross_adr.
  T4 [MEDIUM, BLOCKING] Part of GEOM_OVERLAP has no owner. ADR-0013 § 6 (line 221) defines the GEOM_OVERLAP set as static rects with all flags, plus PLATE slots at full footprint, PLUS the tile cells of every room, tested rect-vs-tile and tile-vs-tile ('two floors on one cell both fail'). ADR-0013's assumption on ADR-0014 says ADR-0014 provides the primitive 'including room tile cells' so the 2 ms uncached target is achievable. ADR-0014 § 7's `footprint_overlaps` and `section_footprints_into` cover only `STATIC_MEMBER` rect rows. Floor tiles are not rows in this table, and nothing in ADR-0014 says how the tile leg is tested or who owns it. Separately, the cost is not quantified. At about 3 us per probe (§ 11, debug binary), the `n_B x cells` probe count for a 2,000-rect body B is around 6 ms in the non-overlapping case, which is the common one because the probe returns early only on a hit. That is above the 2 ms target before the tile leg is added.
    amendment: Choose one option and state it in § 7. (a) The tile leg stays ADR-0013's: a separate floor_tile_at-based check runs after `footprint_overlaps`, and § 7 says so. (b) ADR-0014 adds a per-body floor-cell bitmap or a STATIC_MEMBER-only row class for floor-tile runs, built at rebuild_body, and states how `footprint_overlaps` covers rect-vs-tile and tile-vs-tile. Option (a) is recommended as the smaller change. In either case, add the uncached GEOM_OVERLAP cost at the largest MVP body pair to V4/S1 alongside the rebuild line.
  T5 [LOW] The discard counter rule overrides ADR-0013. ADR-0014 § 6 replaces ADR-0013 § 7/§ 10's 'bump on discard' with `invalidate` (all three counters to 0). ADR-0013's assumption on ADR-0014 says the bump rules are ADR-0013's § 7 and § 8. The override is correct (0 can never alias a live section, and it agrees with ADR-0013 § 11's 'version 0 for an unknown section'), and ADR-0014 declares it. Until ADR-0013 ratifies it, though, the two Proposed documents disagree on the closed caller list.
    amendment: No change to ADR-0014 beyond keeping the declared deviation. ADR-0013 ratifies it (cross_adr).
  T6 [LOW] The restore wording is imprecise for discarded sections. § 6 and § Validation say 'restore: all 1 and version_epoch + 1'. A section discarded before the save must still read 0 after restore, and new_epoch() is not stated to clear the `changed_region` stamp_tick. post_restore stamps ALL on live sections, so this is masked for those sections only. A stamp left over from the pre-restore timeline whose stamp_tick equals the restored T could still be read for any section post_restore does not stamp.
    amendment: Change the wording to 'restore: every LIVE section's three counters set to 1, every other section 0'. Add to `new_epoch()`: 'and resets every changed_region stamp_tick to -1'.
  T7 [LOW] The `## @hot` tag list is incomplete. `RectIndex.set_extent` and `set_empty` run every tick from `layout.doors`, and Key Interfaces comments them as '# hot', but § Implementation Guidelines and § 9 omit them from the HOT-01 tag list. `section_footprints_into` is not tagged either; that is acceptable because it is called only from can_attach validate.
    amendment: Add `RectIndex.set_extent` and `set_empty` to the `## @hot` list in Guidelines and § 9, and tag them in Key Interfaces.
  T8 [LOW] `version_epoch` must only gate rebuilds that do not change results. ADR-0017 D11.4 resets its cache in post_restore, so the first W0 after a restore does a cold rebuild that an uninterrupted run does not. If that work is charged against the Emitter's work budget B and the budget defers anything that affects `lit`, a restored run diverges from an uninterrupted one. That breaks the KRN-RST equivalence that ADR-0016 relies on. ADR-0014 introduces the epoch but states no rule limiting what consumers may do with it.
    amendment: Add one Implementation Guideline: 'A version_epoch change may trigger only a cache rebuild whose result is a pure function of persisted state; it must never feed a work budget, a persisted value or an RNG draw.' The ADR-0017 side is in cross_adr.
  T9 [LOW] Right-sizing and gating are honest. The mechanism (one row table, dense CSR grid, stamp-and-insertion dedupe, structural key order, caller-owned buffer, int64 counters plus epoch) fits a solo or small-team MVP. Every wall-clock claim is marked as margin evidence on an editor binary, and acceptance is gated on S1 (SP-ENG-1) together with the ADR-0010 exemption. The engine version is stamped (4.7.2). Post-cutoff APIs (`@abstract`, the 4.7 typed-return override rule, packed element writes) are flagged with V items. All 13 TR rows that name ADR-0014 in requirements-traceability.md appear in one of the three tables. `src/shared/layout/` matches ADR-0010 line 125. The 14 alternatives are genuine. The only nit is the TR-shipbody-037 '+3' versus '+V_RUN' change: the values are equal at V_RUN 3 and the change is already on the sync list, but registry entities.yaml line 9774 also carries '+ 3' and should be added to that list.
    amendment: Add `design/registry/entities.yaml` (the FOOT_BOX_W coupling comment) to the § Migration Plan sync list.
  
  CROSS-ADR RULINGS (binding):
  CT-02 owner ADR-0013 (align: ADR-0011, ADR-0014, ADR-0015): Merges 0011-review item 1 (second half), 0013-review items 2, 11 and 12 (T3), and the RoomSource half of the LayoutViews single-inheritance item. ADR-0013 owns the port signature and the four record types. `LayoutViews` cannot extend several ports. The setup order is circular: Layout is set up first and needs the Graph port, while the Graph's setup needs Layout's `RoomSource`. I checked ADR-0010 section 2: sim-to-sim imports are allowed in any direction at module granularity, so ports that point both ways create no import-matrix problem and nothing needs to move to `src/shared/`.
    amendment: ADR-0013 section 8 port: rename `check_instantiate(views, template_id)` to `check_instantiate_section(views, section_id: int, template_id: String, kind: int) -> StringName`. `can_build` calls it. Section 11 defines four caller-owned records in `src/sim/layout/views/`, following ADR-0014's QueryBuffer precedent: `SectionBases {node_base, edge_base, comp_base}`; `OpeningRead {area, area_max, door_state}`; `SeamOpenings {count, opening_ids: PackedInt32Array preallocated to the template maximum}`; `SectionCounts {nodes, edges, comps, stub_count, tombstoned: bool, next_section_id}` (meaning fixed by CT-03). Section 11 also states: '`LayoutViews` extends `RefCounted` only. It is constructed inside `LayoutModule.setup` and lives for the whole process. Each port is satisfied by a small adapter that delegates to it, with the port's method names. The adapters in `src/sim/layout/` are `LayoutRoomSource extends RoomSource` (`room_volume_tiles` wraps `V`, `room_exposed_tiles` wraps `exposed_tiles`, and both return -1 for an unknown room), `LayoutSolidQuery extends SolidQuery` and `LayoutOccluderSource extends OccluderSource` (ADR-0014). Body's adapters (`LayoutCollide`, the `BodyLayoutPort` implementation) live in `src/sim/body/` (ADR-0015).' List `room_volume_tiles` and `room_exposed_tiles` in Tier H with their sentinels. Setup: `LayoutModule.setup(facet, templates, tuning)` no longer takes the Graph. `layout.room_source()` returns the `LayoutRoomSource`, which the composition root passes to `GraphModule.setup`. `LayoutModule.bind_graph(port: LayoutGraphPort)` is called by the composition root after `GraphModule.setup` and before the registry freeze; a port call before `bind_graph` is an asserted defect. Add `LayoutRoomSource` and `bind_graph` to the section 1 source layout and the composition-root injection list, and update the architecture.md section 8 step 4 note. Fix the section 3 table: there is no 'comp counter'; a cid is a COMPARTMENT node id taken from `next_node_id`; opening ids are edge ids from `next_edge_id`, not from `next_seam_id`.
  CT-15 owner ADR-0013 (align: ADR-0014): Merges 0013-review item 13 (T7) and 0014-review item 7 (T5). ADR-0014 replaces LM4's version bump with `LayoutVersions.invalidate` (all counters set to 0) and adds `version_epoch` as the restore signal. ADR-0013 must reflect both.
    amendment: ADR-0013 sections 7 and 10: replace 'bump on discard' with 'invalidate (all three counters to 0, `LayoutVersions.invalidate`)'. Add `new_epoch()` to the restore and default_state steps, and cite `version_epoch` as the authoritative restore signal (ADR-0014). Add a GDD sync item for LY-12 d.
  CT-16 owner ADR-0013 (align: ADR-0014, ADR-0021): Merges the 0014-review GEOM_OVERLAP item and ADR-0014 T4. The tile-cell leg has no owner. Option (a), the smaller change, is chosen: it stays ADR-0013's.
    amendment: ADR-0013 section 6: 'The tile-cell leg of GEOM_OVERLAP (rect-vs-tile and tile-vs-tile) is Layout's own `floor_tile_at`-based check, run after ADR-0014 `footprint_overlaps` returns no rect hit.' ADR-0014 section 7 records that option (a) was chosen, and V4/S1 gains an uncached GEOM_OVERLAP line, both legs, at the largest MVP body pair, against ADR-0013's `can_attach` target of 2 ms or less.
  CT-17 owner ADR-0013 (align: ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0017, ADR-0034): Merges the 0013-review 'reads owed' item (T5), the `body_state` ask in the 0015-review BM3 item, and the 0017-review `node_base` and emitter-placement item. Siblings consume reads that ADR-0013 section 11 does not publish. They go in one table.
    amendment: ADR-0013 section 11 adds a table 'Reads owed to Core siblings' with signatures and tiers: `body_is_live(body_id) -> bool` (state == LIVE) and `body_state(body_id) -> int` (LIVE/DISSOLVED/UNKNOWN) for ADR-0015 (Tier H, Tier S after restore); `section_contains(section_id, x, y) -> bool` for ADR-0015; `node_base(section_id) -> int` (0 = NONE, Class 1, valid after restore) for ADR-0017; the frozen SectionTemplates emitter-placement accessors `emitter_placement_count(template_id)` and indexed scalar getters `placement_def_id`, `placement_anchor_x`, `placement_anchor_y`, `placement_node_ordinal`, `placement_switch_on`, `placement_subkind`, loaded at stage 1 with the template schema and validated against ItemCatalog `emits`, for ADR-0017 E1; the `RectFlags` file and the `SlotFeed` for ADR-0014; and `room_volume_tiles`/`room_exposed_tiles` (CT-02). Each Tier H read is tagged `## @hot`.
  CT-18 owner ADR-0014 (align: ADR-0034, ADR-0013): Merges 0014-review item 5 (T3), the 0013-review section_rects_into frame item, and the 0034-review section_rects_into item (ADR-0034 T1). ADR-0014's body-frame, occupied-span contract is consistent with ADR-0013 section 5, so ADR-0034 is the assumer that is wrong. ADR-0014 must still add the key-to-idx read, because `/` and `%` are banned outside IntMath.
    amendment: ADR-0014: add `@abstract func idx_of_key(key: int) -> int` to `OccluderSource`, implemented with IntMath against the stride. Section 5 adds: '`section_rects_into` rows are in the body frame, so a section-scene consumer subtracts `section_offset_x/_y(section_id)`. A row whose current extent is empty is omitted, so the consumer hides that sprite. The kind (JAMB, PLATE, LEAF and so on) is derived from the reserved idx ranges of ADR-0013 section 5.' ADR-0034 sections 5 and 7 and its cross-ADR assumption: call `section_rects_into(section_id, mask, out)`. Rows are body frame, occupied spans (width = span + 1), and `idx = idx_of_key(key)`. Convert to section-local once at build, and store each sprite's section-local rect. On build, mount, weld, cut and re-base, write `position = section_offset(section_id) + local_origin` through `Placement.put`, recomputed from the current offset and never by adding a delta. A staged scene whose section received a BODY or SEC key during its build recomputes positions at commit. Add a weld test in which a socket sprite is built in the same frame as the weld. ADR-0013 lists the body-frame exception in its section 5 frame rule.
  CT-19 owner ADR-0015 (align: ADR-0014, ADR-0023): Merges 0014-review items 1 and 3, 0015-review items 1 and 6, ADR-0014 T1 and ADR-0015 T3. ADR-0014 owns the Layout-side query: `SolidQuery.solid_in(body_id, ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1, out) -> int` with inclusive occupied `spans`. ADR-0015 keeps `CollideSource` as the Body-side seam, because Horror reuses `LocomotionStep`. It drops the stateful `bind`, so body_id is explicit, as ADR-0014 section 5 argues. # Global instructions (all projects)

## Dynamic Workflows: model choice

- Always use Sonnet 5.5 (`model: 'sonnet'`) or Haiku (`model: 'haiku'`) for worker agents in Dynamic Workflows (the Workflow tool's `agent()` calls), to preserve token usage. Use Haiku for mechanical stages (logging, formatting, simple extraction) and Sonnet for the rest.
- Opus or Fable is acceptable only as an advisor where needed: a senior reviewer, judge or verdict seat, never for bulk work such as planners, writers, fixers or scanners.
- Set `model` explicitly on every worker `agent()` call; do not let workers inherit the session model.

# Claude Code Game Studios -- Game Studio Agent Architecture

Indie game development managed through 49 coordinated Claude Code subagents.
Each agent owns a specific domain, enforcing separation of concerns and quality.

## Technology Stack

- **Engine**: Godot 4.7.2
- **Language**: GDScript
- **Version Control**: Git with trunk-based development
- **Build System**: SCons (engine), Godot Export Templates
- **Asset Pipeline**: Godot Import System + custom resource pipeline

> **Note**: Engine-specialist agents exist for Godot, Unity, and Unreal with
> dedicated sub-specialists. Use the set matching your engine.

## Project Structure

@.claude/docs/directory-structure.md

## Engine Version Reference

@docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md


## Technical Preferences

`project.yaml` at the repo root is the primary config store — engine, specialists,
naming, platform, performance, modes. Skills resolve it via `resolve_config`
(see `.claude/docs/config-resolution.md`).

`.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` is the **legacy fallback**, read on demand
when a key is absent from `project.yaml`. It is not imported here: before
`/setup-engine` runs it is almost entirely `[TO BE CONFIGURED]` placeholders, and
after it runs `project.yaml` holds the real values.

## Coordination Rules

@.claude/docs/coordination-rules.md

## Collaboration Protocol

**User-driven collaboration, not autonomous execution.**
Every task follows: **Question -> Options -> Decision -> Draft -> Approval**

- Agents MUST ask "May I write this to [filepath]?" before using Write/Edit tools
  (exempt: `active.md` appends, agent memory, a subagent's new file at the path
  its orchestrating skill named; see `.claude/rules/agent-memory.md`)
- Agents MUST show drafts or summaries before requesting approval
- Multi-file changes require explicit approval for the full changeset
- No commits without user instruction
- A skipped or dismissed question is not an answer: act on nothing, re-ask in
  plain text and wait
- Started outside this file's folder? Warn first: hooks, deny rules and the
  ask-first mode load only when Claude Code starts here

See `docs/COLLABORATIVE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLE.md` for full protocol and examples.

> **First session?** If the project has no engine configured and no game concept,
> run `/start` to begin the guided onboarding flow.

## Coding Standards

@.claude/docs/coding-standards.md

## Context Management

Read `.claude/docs/context-management.md` on demand — it is a reference, not
session context. Two of its conventions are load-bearing and cited by name
elsewhere in the repo, so they are restated here rather than lost:

- **`production/session-state/active.md` is the session checkpoint.** The file is
  the memory, not the conversation. Read it first after any compaction, crash, or
  `/clear`.
- **Helpers in `.claude/scripts/` emit observations, never verdicts.** A script
  that scores or judges will eventually contradict a mode or override it cannot
  see. (Cited by `artifact-check.sh` and `adr-dep-graph.sh`.)

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Godot Engine — Version Reference

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine Version** | Godot 4.7 |
| **Installed at pin time** | 4.7.2.stable.mono.official.ed1daf0bf (matches pin; probed 2026-10-25 at `C:/Users/dasbl/Documents/Godot/`). 4.6.2 standard is also installed, unused. |
| **Release Date** | June 2026 (latest patch: 4.7.2, August 2026) |
| **Project Pinned** | 2026-10-17 |
| **Last Docs Verified** | 2026-10-17 (release timeline and 4.7 changes); 2026-02-12 (4.4-4.6 content) |
| **LLM Knowledge Cutoff** | May 2025 |

## Knowledge Gap Warning

The LLM's training data likely covers Godot up to ~4.3. Versions 4.5, 4.6
and 4.7 were released after the cutoff and introduced significant changes that
the model does NOT know about; 4.4 came out shortly before it and may be thinly
covered. Always cross-reference this directory before suggesting Godot API calls.

## Installed-Version Gap Warning

The warning above is one-directional — it covers the **model** knowing less than
this pin. The reverse gap is real and `/setup-engine` §3 creates it deliberately
("pin the newer one and upgrade later"): this reference can sit **ahead of the
installed editor**, and an agent citing it correctly then emits APIs that do not
compile locally. **Check `Installed at pin time` above before trusting a
version-qualified claim** — `NOT DETERMINED` means the gap is unknown, not absent.

## Post-Cutoff Version Timeline

| Version | Release | Risk Level | Key Theme |
|---------|---------|------------|-----------|
| 4.5 | Sep 2025 | HIGH | Accessibility (AccessKit), variadic args, @abstract, shader baker, SMAA |
| 4.6 | Jan 2026 | HIGH | Jolt default, glow rework, D3D12 default on Windows, IK restored |
| 4.7 | Jun 2026 | HIGH | AreaLight3D, HDR output, Asset Store replaces the Asset Library, VirtualJoystick, Jolt soft-body and world-boundary changes, typed-return overrides |

## Before the Cutoff

4.4 (Mar 2025, Jolt option, FileAccess return types) predates the May 2025
cutoff; the Knowledge Gap Warning still applies to it.

Dates from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases, checked 2026-10-17:
4.4 Mar 3 2025, 4.5 Sep 15 2025, 4.6 Jan 26 2026, 4.7 Jun 18 2026, 4.7.2 Aug 18
2026. Migration guides and release notes: `breaking-changes.md` § Sources.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag
- [Consistency-check needs a confirming run](consistency-check-confirming-run.md) — owner+registry fixes leave leftovers in consumer GDDs; grep referenced_by docs, print patch counts

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag

<system-reminder>
# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.
</system-reminder>

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:

- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.
